connections.why: Cell-membrane structure governs what crosses by diffusion, osmosis and active transport
Mitosis must faithfully copy the cell's organelles and DNA
Meiosis (gametes) and mitosis (growth) are the two ways cells divide
Glucose made in photosynthesis is the fuel respiration releases as ATP
Leaves are the plant organs adapted to maximise photosynthesis
The circulatory system delivers oxygen and glucose to respiring cells
Specialised cells build the tissues and organs of the digestive and circulatory systems
Monoclonal antibodies are engineered to bind specific pathogen antigens
Plants face pathogens too, with physical and chemical defences
The nervous system is one mechanism that keeps internal conditions stable
Hormones give slower, longer-lasting homeostatic control such as blood glucose
Nervous and hormonal systems coordinate the body on different timescales
Meiosis and sexual reproduction create the variation natural selection acts on
Our modern model of inheritance and evolution built on Mendel's work
Evolutionary relationships determine how organisms are classified
Adaptations let organisms compete for niches within an ecosystem
Human activity disrupts the food webs and cycles that organise ecosystems
Trophic levels quantify how energy and biomass move through the ecosystem
Sustainable food production aims to feed people while limiting biodiversity loss
Photosynthesis fixes the energy that then flows through every trophic level
